cohort: The study included 80 neonates admitted to a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit within 24 hours of birth.
finding: Preterm delivery and low birth weight were identified as important risk factors for Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS), which affected 45% of neonates and was associated with increased death rates and longer NICU stays.
mod_finding: Vaginally delivered babies showed a higher incidence of RDS (63.75%) compared to those delivered via caesarean section.
birth_weight: Low birth weight (as a risk factor, no specific ranges given)
gest_age: Preterm and full-term (no specific weeks mentioned)
